mizo_rule_decisions.reviewer_basis: Plural marker on nouns and nominalised forms (fa-te, mi-te, unau-te). Exceptions are diminutive -te forms and a place name.
Nominaliser forming abstract, locative and instrument nouns from verb stems (hriat-na, awm-na, ropui-na). Exceptions are names and hmana 'formerly'.
Ergative/instrumental case marker and adverbial subordinator (pathian-in, avâng-in, tûr-in). Many roots end in -in, so the rule needs a lexicon check; lovin is lo + in with a glide.
Locative case marker (hnên-ah, chung-ah, khua-ah). Stem II verb forms and roots ending in -ah are the main false matches and are listed as exceptions.
Not a suffix: -ng is the final consonant of the root syllable (thleng, chhûng, mihring).
Not a suffix: a mix of Biblical name endings (matthaia, jeremia), root-final -ia (hmeichhia) and hnuai + a.
Agentive nominaliser, 'one who does' (siam-tu, hruai-tu, vêng-tu). hotu 'leader' is lexicalised and kept whole.
Not a suffix: root-final in pathian, tichuan, kristian. In lalpan the real marker is ergative -n after a vowel, not -an.
Not a suffix: -ak is the rhyme of the root syllable (chhuak, tak, ziak).
False segmentation of the causative -tîr; covered by the tîr rule.
Causative verbal suffix (lan-tîr, hriat-tîr, awm-tîr). zirtîr 'teach' is lexicalised and should not merge with zir 'learn'.
False segmentation: stem-final u plus plural -te (unau-te, hotu-te). Covered by the te rule.
False segmentation: stem-final h plus plural -te (thlah-te, tirhkoh-te). Covered by the te rule.
False segmentation: stem II final h plus nominaliser -na (theih-na, thih-na). Covered by the na rule.
False segmentation: stem-final a plus plural -te (fapa-te, juda-te). Covered by the te rule.
Benefactive/applicative verbal suffix, 'do for or to someone' (siam-sak, lâk-sak, tih-sak). Exceptions are lexicalised forms and hmasak 'first'.
False segmentation: stem-final a plus locative -ah (khua-ah, krista-ah). Covered by the ah rule.

Comitative verbal suffix, 'do together with' (kal-pui, awm-pui). The augmentative noun suffix -pui changes the meaning (khaw 'village' vs khawpui 'city'), so those nouns and lexicalised ṭanpui 'help' are exceptions.
False segmentation: stem-final n plus nominaliser -na (chên-na, thlamuan-na). Covered by the na rule.
Not a suffix: -ang is the rhyme of the root syllable (chutiang, chuang, naupang).
Stacked agentive -tu plus plural -te (hruai-tu-te, rorêl-tu-te). Removed together, before the single-suffix rules.
Stacked nominaliser -na plus locative -ah (awm-na-ah, hriat-na-ah). Removed together, before the single-suffix rules.
Mostly false: stem-final -ah plus plural -te (thlah-te, chhuah-te, fahrah-te). Genuine locative + plural cases (hmun-ah-te) are handled by the te and ah rules in turn.
Stacked nominaliser -na plus plural -te (zawh-na-te, harsat-na-te). Removed together, before the single-suffix rules.
False segmentation: root-final ng plus plural -te (zawng-te, mihring-te). Covered by the te rule.
False segmentation: root-final ng plus -in (avâng-in, aṭang-in, hmang-in). Covered by the in rule.
Stacked nominaliser -na plus ergative/instrumental -in (rin-na-in, hmangaih-na-in). Removed together, before the single-suffix rules.
False segmentation: root-final ng plus locative -ah (chung-ah, tlâng-ah, kawng-ah). Covered by the ah rule.
False segmentation: stem II final h plus causative -tîr (neih-tîr, hmuh-tîr). Covered by the tîr rule.
Not Mizo: English loanword ending (station, election). Outside the scope of Mizo suffix rules.
Stacked comitative -pui plus plural -te (kal-pui-te, rin-pui-te). Augmentative nouns are exceptions so that only -te is removed from them by the te rule.
Not Mizo: English loanword ending (education, association). Outside the scope of Mizo suffix rules.
False segmentation of chhuah 'come/bring out', a lexical verb in compounds (puan-chhuah, tih-chhuah); removing it changes the meaning.
False segmentation: stem-final h plus -na-ah (hrilh-na-ah, hmangaih-na-ah). Covered by the naah rule.
False segmentation: stem-final h plus -na-te (zawh-na-te, theih-na-te). Covered by the nate rule.
Stacked agentive -tu, plural -te and ergative -n (rorêl-tu-te-n, hruai-tu-te-n). Longest stack, removed first.
False segmentation: root-final -ang plus -in (chutiang-in, naupang-in). Covered by the in rule.
False segmentation: root-final -ang plus plural -te (naupang-te, apiang-te). Covered by the te rule.
Derivational suffix forming 'causing the feeling of' adjectives from verb stems (zah-thlâk, râp-thlâk, ngaih-thlâk).
False segmentation: stem-final h plus -tu-te (thlah-tu-te, hmangaih-tu-te). Covered by the tute rule.
